# Toast

A short message that confirms an action and goes away.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill odv-pill-out">Left out of Accessible first</span> A toast goes away. Here errors and important notes stay on the page, because people must know what went wrong and where. <span class="odv-instead">Use instead: <a href="./alert">Alert</a></span></p>

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** Saved, sent, exported: something people should notice without stopping.
- **Not when:** A failure people must understand (alert or dialog), or a notice that stays (alert).

Instead:

- [Alert](./alert.md): Stays on the page.
- [Dialog](./dialog.md): Needs an answer.

## How Accessible first uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">The words of an error</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Say what is wrong, where, and exactly how to fix it</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> &quot;Invalid input&quot;</div></div><div class="cap">People must be able to fix the error without help. Example: “Enter your date of birth. For example, 27 3 1980.”</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">A success message</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Confirm what happened and what comes next</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A confirmation with no next step</div></div><div class="cap">People need to know the task is finished and what happens now. Example: “We have your application. We will email you within 5 working days.”</div></div></div>

## Words

- Use common words. Explain any term you must use.
- One idea per sentence. Put the action first.
- Never blame the person.
- Use: Continue, Change, Start, You. Avoid: Invalid, Utilise, Submit, Error code.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Continue
- `content.action.cancel`: Go back
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Start a new application

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It is announced politely without taking focus, and stays long enough to read. undefined
- [ ] Nothing people must act on lives only in a toast. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add toast
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Toast reads 17 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Toast's tokens to change Toast alone.
